headline: The feasibility claim is UPHELD and both solver statuses are provably wrong, but C_illcond_1e10 is NOT a capability gap: the defect is an unnormalised objective, and any norm-based scaling of C makes CLARABEL return the optimum on all 10 seeds and every spread 1e4..1e14. A purchase may not cite this instance.

findings.finding: The load-bearing feasibility claim survives attack. X = I/m is not merely feasible but STRICTLY feasible (Slater), and the feasible set is compact, so the optimum exists, is finite and is attained. CLARABEL's 'infeasible_inaccurate' and SCS's 'unbounded' are therefore both provably wrong answers, not defensible readings of a degenerate problem.
findings.evidence: trace(I/30) = 1.0 exactly; min eig(I/30 - 1e-6 I) = 0.03333233 > 0. X >= 1e-6 I > 0 with trace X = 1 bounds the feasible set. Closed form: X = eps*I + Y, Y psd, trace Y = 1 - m*eps, so p* = eps*trace(C) + (1 - m*eps)*lambda_min(C) = 18250.35288865741; verified by constructing X* = eps*I + (1-m*eps) v_min v_min^T, which satisfies trace X* = 1.0 and min eig(X* - eps I) = -2.6e-17, attaining trace(C X*) = 18250.35288886.

findings.finding: The instance IS badly posed, but not where Techne looked. The defect is objective scaling: C's coefficients span 1e0 to 1e10 while the constraint data is O(1), and neither CVXPY nor CLARABEL/SCS auto-scales the cost. This measures a missing PREPROCESSING STEP in the free path, not a missing solver capability. Normalising C by any norm -- an argmin-preserving one-line change -- closes the 'gap' for $0.
findings.evidence: Rescaled by lambda_max: CLARABEL 'optimal', 18255.16 (rel err 2.6e-4) in 53 ms; recomputed trace(C X) from the returned X agrees at 18255.1577, with trace X = 1.000000000000 and min eig(X - eps I) = -2.2e-10. Robust to the normaliser: lambda_max 2.6e-4, Frobenius 2.8e-4, max|C_ij| 5.9e-4, trace(C) 1.9e-3, round 1e10 2.6e-4 -- all 'optimal'. Holds on all 10 seeds at 1e10 and at spreads 1e4, 1e6..1e14.
findings.required_fix: Normalise the objective in pm.optimization.solve_sdp (divide C by ||C|| and multiply the returned value back) before any instance is called a failure. Re-run the fixture with that in place.

findings.finding: One reposing does NOT rescue it, which localises the defect: the variable-shift substitution X = eps I + Y (Y psd, trace Y = 1 - m eps) still returns CLARABEL 'infeasible' and SCS 'unbounded'. So the eps-floor constraint is not the problem; the magnitude of the cost coefficients is.
findings.evidence: R2 (shift only): CLARABEL infeasible, SCS unbounded. R3 (shift + scale): both optimal, CLARABEL rel err 2.6e-4. Scaling is necessary and sufficient; the shift is neither.

findings.finding: MISSING WEAKNESS, and the most serious one available here: the fixture's failure criterion is status-only (p.status not in ('optimal',)), so it is structurally blind to a solver that returns a confidently wrong NUMBER. SCS does exactly that. After normalisation SCS reports status 'optimal' and returns 52618 against a true optimum of 18250 -- 188% wrong -- and the fixture as written would score that a PASS. At 1e4 the fixture scored SCS a failure only because SCS happened to say 'optimal_inaccurate'; the same 1.3%-wrong number under an 'optimal' status would have passed.
findings.evidence: Post-normalisation SCS rel err by spread (all status 'optimal'): 1e4 1.15e-1, 1e6 3.44e0, 1e7 2.14e0, 1e8 4.05e0, 1e10 1.88e0, 1e12 1.41e0, 1e14 2.05e0. All 10 seeds at 1e10: 1.88e0, status 'optimal'.
findings.required_fix: Score on |value - p*|/p* against a declared ground truth, with status as secondary evidence. A silent wrong answer is a worse defect than a loud failure status and must not be able to pass.

findings.finding: The declared ground truth is the wrong kind of object. a_feasible_point_attains = trace(C)/m is the value at the Slater point -- a loose UPPER BOUND, 33,331x the true optimum at 1e10 and 1,182x at 1e4 -- yet it is the fixture's only numerical anchor. This family has a closed-form optimum available in one line, and the fixture does not use it. Consequence: the fixture can detect status failures only, never value failures.
findings.evidence: p*(1e10) = 18250.3529 vs declared 608311763.96 (ratio 33331.5). p*(1e4) = 1.0367178960 vs declared 1224.93 (ratio 1182). Against the closed form, the fixture's own 1e4 numbers resolve cleanly: CLARABEL rel err 3.3e-9 (correct), SCS rel err 1.33e-2 (wrong) -- a resolution the fixture could not state.
findings.required_fix: Replace a_feasible_point_attains with p_star = eps*trace(C) + (1 - m*eps)*lambda_min(C), and report each solver's relative error against it.

findings.finding: SELECTION ARTIFACT: the headline 'every free solver failed' depends on an unreported hardcoded seed. seed=7 is baked into _ill_conditioned and never surfaced in the result document. On 2 of 10 seeds from the identical family, CLARABEL solves the UNSCALED problem to 9 significant digits and reports 'optimal' -- on which seeds the case would have been scored a pass and no candidate gap would exist.
findings.evidence: seed 4: status optimal, 18250.352781533264, rel err 5.9e-9. seed 5: status optimal, 18250.35285685584, rel err 1.8e-9. Remaining 8 seeds scatter across infeasible (4), infeasible_inaccurate (1), unbounded_inaccurate (1) and a raised SolverError (2) -- five distinct failure modes for one problem shape, which is itself the signature of a scaling heuristic tipping, not of a capability boundary.
findings.required_fix: Report the seed in the result document and run every gap case over a seed family; a regime claim needs the distribution, not one draw.

findings.finding: UNDERCLAIM, and the only route by which a purchase could ever be argued: the fixture declares no ACCURACY REQUIREMENT, so 'failure' is undefined and no spend can be justified from it either way. After normalisation the free path is not perfect -- CLARABEL delivers ~7.4 significant digits at cond 1e2 but only ~3.2-3.6 from cond 1e6 upward. Whether 3.5 digits at cond 1e10 is a failure is a requirements question nobody has answered, and it is the only question in this file that could bear on $4,300.
findings.evidence: CLARABEL post-normalisation rel err by spread (seed 7): 1e2 4.4e-8, 1e4 1.7e-6, 1e6 6.8e-4, 1e8 7.0e-4, 1e10 2.6e-4, 1e12 3.2e-4.
findings.required_fix: State the required relative accuracy for pm.optimization.solve_sdp and the conditioning our problems actually exhibit, BEFORE any further gap case is built. Note the fixture's own text already anticipates the answer: if the requirement is a verifiable certificate rather than a fast float, no double-precision solver satisfies it at any price and the route is arbitrary precision at $0.

answers_to_commission.q1_verdict: BADLY POSED -- but the feasibility claim Techne was asked to defend is correct. The problem is feasible, strictly so, and bounded; both solver statuses are wrong answers. The instance nonetheless fails for a reason Techne did not see: an unnormalised objective, which is a defect of the posing and of the free path's preprocessing, not of solver capability.
answers_to_commission.q2_defect_and_reposing: Defect: cost coefficients spanning 1e10 with no scaling. Reposings that STILL fail both solvers: none found -- the variable shift alone still fails, but every norm-based scaling of C succeeds. CLARABEL returns the optimum under all five normalisers tried, on all 10 seeds, at spreads 1e4 through 1e14.
answers_to_commission.q3_does_one_instance_license_gap: Moot here -- there is no genuine failure to license. For the record: one instance never licenses 'gap', and this one is weaker than one, because it is seed-dependent (2 of 10 seeds solve unscaled to 9 digits). A purchase needs a family with a declared accuracy requirement, measured AFTER standard normalisation, and a demonstration that the paid solver clears a bar the free path misses.
answers_to_commission.may_a_purchase_cite_this: NO. C_illcond_1e10 is withdrawn as evidence about any solver. REQ-029's MOSEK row remains a roadmap item with no measured need, which by TECHNE-37's own rule means no authorisation to spend.
answers_to_commission.techne_caveat_status: CONFIRMED and then some -- the caveat said the instance MAY be badly posed; it is, and the fixture also cannot see the one real defect it exposed (SCS's silent 188% error under an 'optimal' status).

spot_checks.what: X = I/m satisfies trace X = 1 and X >> 1e-6 I (Techne's feasibility certificate)
closed-form optimum p* = eps*tr(C) + (1-m*eps)*lambda_min(C), verified by explicit construction of X* attaining it
reproduction of the reported failure as posed, cvxpy 1.9.2, same solver set
objective rescaling by lambda_max, Frobenius, max|C_ij|, trace(C), round 1e10
returned X re-checked independently: trace, min eigenvalue of X - eps I, and trace(C X) recomputed outside the solver
10-seed family sweep at spread 1e10 and spread sweep 1e4..1e14
the fixture's own 1e4 numbers scored against the closed form
whether MOSEK solves the unscaled instance

reviewer_limits: No MOSEK licence here, so the counterfactual 'a paid solver would have solved it unscaled' is untested. It is also not load-bearing: the free path solves it once scaled, so the paid counterfactual cannot justify a spend either way.
All results are from this machine's cvxpy 1.9.2 / CLARABEL / SCS build at base_sha ad94bf2eb. Solver-version-dependent behaviour (particularly the five scattered failure modes) may differ elsewhere.
